$comment: Constraints and invariants every agent must obey. Owner of each rule is its 'owner' (a canonical repository file); this file is the continuity index of those rules, not a second constitution.

records.title: External side effects need authorization
records.statement: No commit, push, merge, release, deployment, billing change or other external write without the owner's authorization for that action.

records.title: Configuration over code
records.statement: Features, providers, vocabularies and runtime backends are entity/config data, never code branches; features ship OFF by default and are enabled by writing configuration.

records.title: Prefer the standard library
records.statement: Prefer Node's standard library and existing code; a new dependency needs a justified trade-off.

records.title: No claim without observed evidence
records.statement: Never report a test as passed, a feature as implemented or a state as verified unless the command ran or the inspection happened and its result was observed and recorded; a plan, prompt or generated file is not an implementation.

records.title: Law 005 — Explainability
records.statement: Every artifact must answer what happened, who authorized it, which policy allowed it, what evidence supports it, and with what confidence.

records.title: 27 frozen primitives
records.statement: The 27 primitives in _registry/primitives.json are frozen; none may be added without constitutional amendment and proof of mathematical unavoidability.

records.title: Law 002 — Knowledge Once
records.statement: Every artifact id, primitive and canonical term is defined exactly once; every concept has one canonical owner, and everything else references or derives from it.

records.title: No loss of unique knowledge
records.statement: Unique requirements, decisions, constraints, rationale, evidence and unresolved issues are never deleted or summarised away; retirement is a lifecycle transition with approval, and consolidation must map every unique item to its destination.

records.title: Private conversation archives stay out of git
records.statement: Private conversation exports and attachments are archived only in access-controlled storage (CONTEXT_ARCHIVE_DIR); the repository holds their manifest metadata, never their bytes; CI uses synthetic fixtures.

records.title: No credentials in the repository or in derived context
records.statement: Secrets (.env, keys, the keyring, the registry key) are never committed, and never copied into context packs, logs, reports or handoffs.

records.title: Node ≥ 22.13
records.statement: The runtime requires Node 22.13 or newer (built-in node:sqlite); CI runs 22.13, 22 and 24.

records.title: Preserve the owner's working tree
records.statement: Never reset, clean or overwrite uncommitted user changes to make work easier; record them in the baseline and work around them.

records.title: Law 003 — Projection Law
records.statement: Documents are generated from the registry, never authored; editing a projected document directly is a constitutional violation — change the registry and re-project.

records.title: The compiled registry seal is derived, never committed
records.statement: _registry/canonical.json and canonical.lxr are compiled deterministically from the corpora and registry JSON and are not committed; data/registry.json and data/master.json are per-deployment secrets.

records.title: Superseded originals are provenance, not truth
records.statement: Files in _superseded/ (and any record in lifecycle superseded or historical-evidence) are preserved provenance and must never be used as current authority.

records.title: Law 001 — Zero Hard Coding
records.statement: No product, service, offer, contract, currency, country, language, industry or marketplace concept may appear as a schema type; they are runtime projections of configuration.
